answer: Epoch-seeded VRF admission lottery: a threshold-BLS randomness beacon publishes seed S after registration closes. Each key K computes ticket=VRF_K(S); tickets below threshold T yield an admission signal and task slot, with roles derived by hashing into willow/umber domains. Because S is unpredictable until post-registration, attackers cannot precompute winning keys or pre-mint sybils. Flooding requires fresh per-key VRF computation and key management after S, so cost scales linearly with identities, with no bulk shortcut.
